q: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a ____.
e: Circular motion means the object travels on a circular path. The blank is circle, because a straight line or a parabola is a different kind of path.

q: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an ____.
e: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an axis. Rotational motion means a body spins about an axis.

q: A rigid body is a body that does not ____ or change shape.
e: A rigid body is a body that does not deform or change shape. A rigid body keeps a fixed shape, so it does not deform.

q: In a rigid body, no matter how the body moves, the ____ between any two particles within the body remains constant.
e: In a rigid body, no matter how the body moves, the distance between any two particles within the body remains constant. In a rigid body the distance between any two particles stays constant.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo circular motion about a common ____.
e: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo circular motion about a common axis. Rotational motion means a body spins about an axis.

q: When an object (rigid body) rotates, it can speed up (or) ____ down.
e: When an object (rigid body) rotates, it can speed up (or) slow down. A rigid body keeps a fixed shape, so the distance between any two of its particles stays constant.

q: During the time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular ____.
e: During the time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α.

q: If the angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is ____.
e: If the angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is constant. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: Rotational variables include angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular ____.
e: Rotational variables include angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α.

q: The kinematic equations for rotational motion are derived for an object that rotates with a constant angular ____.
e: The kinematic equations for rotational motion are derived for an object that rotates with a constant angular acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α.

q: The magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t=0$ is called the initial angular ____.
e: The magnitude of angular velocity of the object at t=0 is called the initial angular speed. Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in ____ motion.
e: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in linear motion. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: In Grade 10, kinematic equations were derived for linear motion with constant ____.
e: In Grade 10, kinematic equations were derived for linear motion with constant acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α.

q: The linear equation $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$ is analogous to the angular equation $\omega^2 = \omega_0^2 + 2\alpha\____$.
e: The linear equation v² = v₀² + 2as is analogous to the angular equation ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ. θ is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: According to the summary, angular acceleration is constant if the angular velocity changes at a constant ____.
e: According to the summary, angular acceleration is constant if the angular velocity changes at a constant rate. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: Motion with a constant rate of change of angular velocity is called rotational motion under constant angular ____.
e: Motion with a constant rate of change of angular velocity is called rotational motion under constant angular acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α.

q: The summary states that for uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration vector points towards the ____ of the circular path.
e: The summary states that for uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration vector points towards the centre of the circular path. The centre of the circle is where a_C and F_c point.

q: The summary notes that the linear velocity vector is ____ to the circular path.
e: The summary notes that the linear velocity vector is tangential to the circular path. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path.

q: The acceleration directed towards the centre of the circular path is called ____ acceleration.
e: The acceleration directed towards the centre of the circular path is called centripetal acceleration. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle.

q: The angular acceleration is equal to ____ when there is no change in angular velocity.
e: The angular acceleration is equal to zero when there is no change in angular velocity. A limit as Δt → 0 is the instantaneous rate, so that increment goes to zero.

q: The relations between linear quantities and ____ quantities for circular motion were studied in Grade 11.
e: The relations between linear quantities and angular quantities for circular motion were studied in Grade 11. Angular quantities θ, ω and α are the rotational twins of linear s, v and a.

q: All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a ____ path.
e: All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path. Each particle of a rotor travels on a circular path about the axis.

q: All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is ____ to the axis.
e: All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is perpendicular to the axis. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles.

q: For particles in rotational motion, the centre of rotation lies on the ____.
e: For particles in rotational motion, the centre of rotation lies on the axis. Rotational motion means a body spins about an axis.

q: In the equation $s = r \theta$, the variable $r$ represents the ____ of the circle.
e: In the equation s = r θ, the variable r represents the radius of the circle. Radius r links linear and angular measures through s = rθ and v = rω.

q: The instantaneous angular velocity $\omega$ of a rotational object is the ____ for all the particles comprising the object.
e: The instantaneous angular velocity ω of a rotational object is the same for all the particles comprising the object. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: Because its direction is tangent to the path, linear velocity is also called ____ velocity.
e: Because its direction is tangent to the path, linear velocity is also called tangential velocity. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path.

q: If the magnitude of the angular velocity changes, the object will have a ____ acceleration.
e: If the magnitude of the angular velocity changes, the object will have a tangential acceleration. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path.

q: The direction of tangential acceleration is always ____ to the circular path.
e: The direction of tangential acceleration is always tangent to the circular path. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle.

q: Tangential acceleration is a measure of how fast the tangential ____ changes.
e: Tangential acceleration is a measure of how fast the tangential velocity changes. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is ____ to the plane of rotation.
e: The direction of the angular velocity vector is perpendicular to the plane of rotation. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is usually specified by the ____-hand rule.
e: The direction of the angular velocity vector is usually specified by the right-hand rule. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: In the right-hand rule, the fingers are wrapped to point in the direction of ____.
e: In the right-hand rule, the fingers are wrapped to point in the direction of rotation. The right-hand rule sets the sense of the angular velocity vector along the axis.

q: In the right-hand rule, the ____ points in the direction of the angular velocity vector.
e: In the right-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the angular velocity vector. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the ____ direction as the angular velocity.
e: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points ____ to the angular velocity.
e: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points opposite to the angular velocity. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: Angular acceleration $\alpha$ is measured in radian per second ____.
e: Angular acceleration α is measured in radian per second squared. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: The text uses a randomly shaped ____ body to illustrate rotational motion.
e: The text uses a randomly shaped rigid body to illustrate rotational motion. rigid is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: All particles comprising a rotating rigid body share the same instantaneous angular ____.
e: All particles comprising a rotating rigid body share the same instantaneous angular velocity. A rigid body keeps a fixed shape, so the distance between any two of its particles stays constant.

q: The relation $v = r \omega$ applies to ____ particle of the rotational object.
e: The relation v = r ω applies to every particle of the rotational object. The centripetal acceleration formula applies at every point on the circle.

q: A change in the magnitude of angular velocity causes the magnitude of linear velocity to ____.
e: A change in the magnitude of angular velocity causes the magnitude of linear velocity to change. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: An object that moves in a circle at constant speed is said to experience ____ circular motion.
e: An object that moves in a circle at constant speed is said to experience uniform circular motion. Uniform here means constant speed along the circle.

q: In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant, but the ____ of the velocity continuously changes.
e: In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant, but the direction of the velocity continuously changes. On a circle the velocity direction keeps turning even if the speed is steady.

q: The continuous change in the direction of velocity constitutes an ____.
e: The continuous change in the direction of velocity constitutes an acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α.

q: An object revolving in a circle is continuously accelerated, even when its ____ remains constant.
e: An object revolving in a circle is continuously accelerated, even when its speed remains constant. Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

q: Average acceleration is defined as the change in velocity divided by the change in ____.
e: Average acceleration is defined as the change in velocity divided by the change in time. Average angular velocity is angular displacement divided by the time interval.

q: Instantaneous acceleration is obtained when the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches ____.
e: Instantaneous acceleration is obtained when the time interval Δ t approaches zero. A limit as Δt → 0 is the instantaneous rate, so that increment goes to zero.

q: During the time interval $\Delta t$, the object covers a distance along the ____ which subtends an angle $\Delta \theta$.
e: During the time interval Δ t, the object covers a distance along the arc which subtends an angle Δ θ. Arc length s is the linear distance along the circle, s = rθ with θ in radians.

q: As $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the angular displacement $\Delta \theta$ becomes very ____.
e: As Δ t approaches zero, the angular displacement Δ θ becomes very small. Angular displacement θ is the angle the body turns, measured in radians in the s = rθ family of equations.

q: When $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the change in velocity $\Delta v$ is essentially ____ to the velocity vectors.
e: When Δ t approaches zero, the change in velocity Δ v is essentially perpendicular to the velocity vectors. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles.

q: The instantaneous acceleration in uniform circular motion points toward the ____ of the circle.
e: The instantaneous acceleration in uniform circular motion points toward the centre of the circle. The centre of the circle is where a_C and F_c point.

q: Acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path is called ____ acceleration.
e: Acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path is called centripetal acceleration. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle.

q: Centripetal acceleration is also called radial acceleration because it is directed along the ____.
e: Centripetal acceleration is also called radial acceleration because it is directed along the radius. Radius r links linear and angular measures through s = rθ and v = rω.

q: The derivation of centripetal acceleration uses the fact that the position triangle is geometrically ____ to the velocity vector triangle.
e: The derivation of centripetal acceleration uses the fact that the position triangle is geometrically similar to the velocity vector triangle. Centripetal acceleration a_C points to the centre of the circle and has magnitude v²/r or rω².

q: Centripetal acceleration is defined as the limit of $\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$ as $\Delta t$ approaches ____.
e: Centripetal acceleration is defined as the limit of (Δ v)/(Δ t) as Δ t approaches zero. A limit as Δt → 0 is the instantaneous rate, so that increment goes to zero.

q: The limit of $\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta t}$ as $\Delta t \to 0$ represents the linear ____ of the object.
e: The limit of (Δ s)/(Δ t) as Δ t to 0 represents the linear speed of the object. Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

q: In uniform circular motion, the linear velocity vector is ____ to the path.
e: In uniform circular motion, the linear velocity vector is tangential to the path. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path.

q: At every point in the path of uniform circular motion, centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are ____ to each other.
e: At every point in the path of uniform circular motion, centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are perpendicular to each other. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles.

q: Nonuniform circular motion is characterized by a varying ____.
e: Nonuniform circular motion is characterized by a varying speed. Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

q: A varying linear speed in circular motion means the angular ____ is changing.
e: A varying linear speed in circular motion means the angular speed is changing. Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

q: Angular acceleration in nonuniform circular motion gives rise to ____ acceleration.
e: Angular acceleration in nonuniform circular motion gives rise to tangential acceleration. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, tangential acceleration exists in addition to ____ acceleration.
e: In nonuniform circular motion, tangential acceleration exists in addition to centripetal acceleration. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle.

q: The resultant acceleration in nonuniform circular motion is the vector ____ of centripetal and tangential accelerations.
e: The resultant acceleration in nonuniform circular motion is the vector sum of centripetal and tangential accelerations. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: Unlike tangential acceleration, ____ acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion.
e: Unlike tangential acceleration, centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle.

q: The vectors for centripetal acceleration and tangential acceleration are ____ to each other.
e: The vectors for centripetal acceleration and tangential acceleration are perpendicular to each other. Perpendicular means the two directions stand at right angles.

q: The centripetal acceleration vector $a_c$ acts in the ____ direction.
e: The centripetal acceleration vector a_c acts in the radial direction. Centripetal acceleration a_C points to the centre of the circle and has magnitude v²/r or rω².

q: The tangential acceleration vector $a_T$ acts in the ____ direction.
e: The tangential acceleration vector a_T acts in the tangential direction. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path.

q: The resultant acceleration vector points at an ____ between $a_c$ and $a_T$.
e: The resultant acceleration vector points at an angle between a_c and a_T. Angle θ in radians is the angular displacement in s = rθ.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the object experiences tangential acceleration which is ____ to the circle.
e: In nonuniform circular motion, the object experiences tangential acceleration which is tangential to the circle. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path.

q: Thus, an object in nonuniform circular motion has a resultant acceleration that is the vector sum of the centripetal and ____ accelerations.
e: Thus, an object in nonuniform circular motion has a resultant acceleration that is the vector sum of the centripetal and tangential accelerations. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path.
